thesis: This episode argues that Limbach (LMB) is a compelling buy because the market has punished it for missing the data center boom, but the speaker believes the business is fundamentally sound and that a new CYMCOR acquisition will finally provide the necessary data center exposure. The guest contends that the EBITDA decline stems from fixed cost deleverage on a temporary demand air pocket rather than a broken business, and that the company is undervalued compared to peers who compounded on data centers. Beyond Limbach, the discussion covers a wide range of other positions, including bullish views on Celsius, Baker Hughes, DoorDash, and Roku, while expressing bearish sentiment on Spotify and Nvidia.

claims.claim: Celsius is undervalued compared to competitors like Monster and Coke despite faster growth.
claims.quote: Celsius trades at ~20x earnings while growing ~18% a year, cheaper than Monster (~34x) and even Coke (~25x) despite faster growth.

claims.claim: The market hasn't fully appreciated Baker Hughes' evolution from a cyclical oil field services business.
claims.quote: Team Baker Hughes, the second-place finishers in the 2026 Pershing Square Challenge, discuss their Baker Hughes thesis and why they believe the market hasn't fully appreciated the company's evolution from a cyclical oil field services business.

claims.claim: DoorDash's growth story still has room to run with durable US restaurant growth and new verticals.
claims.quote: The winners of the Pershing Square Challenge 2026 discuss their Doordash pitch, including why the growth story still has room to run (and the 90 primary research calls they made to back up that call).

claims.claim: Take 5 remains a crown jewel and could be worth the entire EV of the company.
claims.quote: Kyle Mowery (GrizzlyRock Capital) walks through why Take 5 remains a crown jewel and could be worth the entire EV of the company (making the franchise and autoglass businesses a free option).

claims.claim: Liberty Global is cheap on a sum-of-the-parts basis with an upcoming Ziggo spin to crystallize value.
claims.quote: Rich Howe of Stock Spin-Off Investing makes the bull case for Liberty Global ($LBTYK): cheap on a sum-of-the-parts, an upcoming Ziggo spin to crystallize value, and a hidden ventures portfolio.

claims.claim: The guest argues MSA is an underrated quality compounder with a strong bull case, while the host pushes back on the valuation and timeline.
claims.quote: MSA Safety ($MSA) is the "OG pick and shovel" of worker safety: a century-old, pure-play maker of gas detection and firefighter equipment that the Pershing Square Challenge 2026 finalist team argues is a quality compounder the market is underrating. The bull case has three legs.

claims.claim: The host questions whether the market is inefficient or if the business is simply priced correctly despite the long-term upside.
claims.quote: I push back on the obvious tension: this is a roughly 20x compounder that does not scream alpha, the CFO is guiding mid-single-digit growth, and most of the thesis only pays off in 2028 to 2030. Is the market that inefficient, or is this just a very good business priced about right?

claims.claim: The guest believes the market is wrong about the Fox-Roku deal being a blunder, while the host questions if the combined entity is better than Roku staying neutral.
claims.quote: Fox's stock is down about 25% since it agreed to buy Roku for $22 billion, and the market has decided the deal is a blunder. Simeon McMillan of Accrued Interest thinks the market is wrong.

claims.claim: The host questions whether the combined Fox and Roku is truly better than Roku remaining neutral to every bidder.
claims.quote: I push back hard on whether Fox plus Roku is really better than Roku staying neutral Switzerland for every bidder.

claims.claim: The guest is bullish on Roku, citing its control of a large share of streaming viewing and its value as a platform.
claims.quote: Roku controls roughly 44% of how Americans reach streaming on the big screen, about 3x the next platform, so Fox just bought the "front door" to streaming and around 100 million connected TVs in North America.

claims.claim: The speaker highlights that Yaron Naymark of 1 Main Capital pitched Limbach in June 2023, watched it 6.5x, sold most of it, and is back buying it after a 75% drawdown.
claims.quote: Yaron Naymark of 1 Main Capital pitched me this name in June 2023, watched it 6.5x, sold most of it, and is back buying it after a 75% drawdown.

claims.claim: The speaker mentions that the stock lost half its value after organic revenue went down mid single digits and EBITDA fell 30%.
claims.quote: Then organic revenue went down mid single digits, EBITDA fell 30%, guidance came down from $90m to $80m, and the stock lost half its value.

claims.claim: The speaker pushes back on the bear case that management knowingly bid a pile of low margin work.
claims.quote: I push back on the bear case that management knowingly bid a pile of low margin work, on whether owner direct is just general contracting by another name, on whether wage inflation from the data center boom is quietly eating them, and on whether a 2016 de-SPAC ever escapes the gravity of $10 per share.
